newsitem.title: UK: Bahrain opposition says 20, mostly children, held.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain opposition says 20, mostly children, held.

text.p: A Bahraini opposition group said on Tuesday that 20 Bahraini Shi'ite Moslems, mostly children, had been arrested in the Gulf state this month in connection with anti-government protests.
The Bahrain Islamic Freedom Movement said in a statement sent to an international news organisation that three children, including six-year-old Sayyed Hussain Reda, were arrested in Adari village.
Three people in Sanabis village, five children in al-Daih village, two in Samaheej village and seven children aged between eight and 15 years in the small island of Sitra had been arrested, it said.
The London-based group did not say why they had been arrested but said another woman from Bilad al-Qadeem was shot and wounded on April 16.
Last month, the group said Bahrain had arrested 19 people including children. Bahrain denied the claim.
Members of the island's majority Shi'ite community have waged sporadic protests, bombings amd arson attacks since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government.
Around 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested, including children.
